quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 40 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.
It only protects your eyes.
It protects your whole face.
It does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects your whole face.
questions.explanation: A face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes, not the rest of your face. A windshield is not a good substitute for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: How should a passenger sit on a motorcycle?

options.text: With their feet on the ground when the motorcycle stops.
Without riding unless there is a back rest.
As far forward as possible without blocking the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: As far forward as possible without blocking the driver.
questions.explanation: A passenger should sit as far forward as possible without blocking the driver. Keep both feet on the footrests at all times, even when stopped.

questions.question: Which color makes you less visible to other drivers?

options.text: Orange
Yellow
Brown

questions.correctAnswerText: Brown
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green to be more visible to other drivers. Avoid dark or dull colors while riding.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Yield to other drivers.
A stop sign is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: How should jackets and pants fit when riding?

options.text: Loose enough so the wind catches the fabric.
Snug enough so they do not flap in the wind.
Tight enough to stop you from moving freely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Snug enough so they do not flap in the wind.
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants should fit snugly so they do not flap in the wind, but loose enough that you can move freely.

questions.question: What reduces the risk of head or neck injury?

options.text: Wearing a helmet.
Riding more slowly.
Reading the owner's manual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing a helmet.
questions.explanation: A good helmet greatly reduces the risk of head and neck injuries. Speed does not prevent these injuries. Always wear a quality helmet.

questions.question: What is the best way to help others see your motorcycle?

options.text: Flash your lights.
Keep your high beam headlight on.
Paint your motorcycle a dark color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your high beam headlight on.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on day and night whenever legal and safe. Use your high beam to help others see you better.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Two-way traffic
Right lane ends
Merge

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that traffic is merging.

questions.question: What is true about a DOT-approved helmet?

options.text: It severely limits your vision.
It allows you to see as far to the sides as needed for safe riding.
It can become a hazard to the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: It allows you to see as far to the sides as needed for safe riding.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet does not limit your vision. You can see everything you need to see for safe riding.

questions.question: How should you sit to properly control a motorcycle?

options.text: Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Use your arms to hold up your body.
Keep your knees against the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Sit with your arms slightly bent. Use your arms to steer, not to hold up your body. Keep your knees against the gas tank to help balance during turns.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop completely. Then go when it is safe.
Stop only if other traffic is coming.
Vehicles are entering the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely. Then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop completely. Let all traffic and pedestrians pass. Then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: You must stop completely.
You can go through with caution.
You must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop completely.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red light. You must stop completely. Wait for a green arrow before you turn in that direction.

questions.question: How are convex mirrors different from regular mirrors?

options.text: They show a narrower view of the road.
They show a wider view of the road.
They show a clearer view of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They show a wider view of the road.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors are common on motorcycles. They show a wider view than flat mirrors. However, they can make vehicles behind you look farther away than they really are.

questions.question: You reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle. What should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlights to signal the other vehicle to go.
Continue through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: When you spot a hazard on the road, you should NOT:

options.text: Fail to communicate with other drivers.
Adjust your speed.
Use your horn, lights, or signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fail to communicate with other drivers.
questions.explanation: Tell other drivers you are there by using your horn, lights, and signals. Adjust your speed for safety. Change your lane position or direction as needed.

questions.question: Locking your brakes can:

options.text: Help in most situations.
Make steering better.
Create control problems.

questions.correctAnswerText: Create control problems.
questions.explanation: Locking your brakes can create control problems. If your front brake locks, release it and apply it again right away. If your rear brake locks on good pavement, keep it locked until you stop.

questions.question: When riding in a group, where should less experienced riders be positioned?

options.text: At the front.
Right behind the lead rider.
At the back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right behind the lead rider.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride near the front, right behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them from behind.

questions.question: The Motorcycle Safety Foundation recommends the SEE strategy. What does SEE mean?

options.text: Search, Evaluate, and Execute.
Slow, Experienced, and Error-free.
Safe, Experienced, and Evasive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Search, Evaluate, and Execute.
questions.explanation: Good riders use the SEE strategy to ride safely. SEE stands for Search, Evaluate, and Execute.

questions.question: Small vehicles appear to be ________ and slower than they really are.

options.text: Closer
Farther away
Larger

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge the speed and distance of small vehicles like motorcycles. Do not assume drivers of large vehicles can judge your speed and location correctly.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the roadside with its lights flashing. What should you do?

options.text: Stop on the road behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait for the emergency vehicle to move.
Switch to another lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Switch to another lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside assistance vehicle with lights flashing, change lanes to give it extra space. Slow down and be ready to stop near the emergency scene.

questions.question: What should passengers do?

options.text: Look over their shoulder when the motorcycle turns.
Never hold onto the rider.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over their shoulder when the motorcycle turns.
questions.explanation: Ask your passenger to look over your shoulder in the direction you are turning. This helps you lean the motorcycle correctly.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: On the left side of the lane, near the centerline.
On the right side of the lane, near the curb.
It depends on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position for all situations. Choose the position that gives you the best visibility and most space around you. Change your position as traffic changes.

questions.question: What about taking over-the-counter medication before riding?

options.text: It is usually fine because over-the-counter medications are not very strong.
It is always acceptable.
It may affect your riding ability and should be done carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may affect your riding ability and should be done carefully.
questions.explanation: Many medications, including over-the-counter drugs, can affect your ability to ride safely. Talk to your doctor about how any new medication may affect your riding.

questions.question: What does a solid white line on the side of the road mean?

options.text: No parking is allowed.
It marks the right edge of the traffic lane.
Traffic must merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: It marks the right edge of the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of the traffic lane.

questions.question: When is there less traction available for braking?

options.text: When the motorcycle is leaning.
When the motorcycle is straight up and down.
When the motorcycle is on dry pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the motorcycle is leaning.
questions.explanation: When a motorcycle leans during a turn, there is less traction for braking. You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while stopping on good pavement, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and then quickly apply it again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks up while stopping on good pavement, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can still control your motorcycle if it is upright and moving straight.

questions.question: What should motorcyclists do about the oily strip in the center of a traffic lane?

options.text: Avoid riding on the oil and grease.
Do not worry about the oil and grease.
Find the lane with the least amount of oil and grease.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid riding on the oil and grease.
questions.explanation: Avoid the oily strip in the center of the lane. Since the oily strip is usually only about two feet wide, you can ride on the left or right side of it and still be in the center part of the lane.

questions.question: If you are passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic, where should you ride?

options.text: In the left portion of your lane.
In the right portion of your lane.
In the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane. This helps you avoid hazards like opening car doors and pedestrians stepping out. If there is oncoming traffic, stay in the center of your lane to have more space around you.

questions.question: What is true about the front brake?

options.text: Use it only when you need to stop quickly.
Use it only on slippery surfaces.
It is less effective than the rear brake.
It is safe to use if used properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is safe to use if used properly.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes whenever you slow down or stop. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake, but it is safe to use if you use it correctly.

questions.question: What lane position should you choose?

options.text: One that makes you visible and gives you safe space around you.
Any position you like, regardless of other vehicles.
One that gets you close to other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: One that makes you visible and gives you safe space around you.
questions.explanation: Choose a position where you can be seen and where you have space around your motorcycle. There is no single best position for all situations. Change your position as conditions change.

questions.question: What do convex mirrors do?

options.text: Show a narrow view of the road behind you.
Show a wide view of the road behind you.
Are illegal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show a wide view of the road behind you.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors. They make objects look farther away than they really are. Get used to your mirrors if your motorcycle has them.

questions.question: Before you start riding, make sure the fuel valve is:

options.text: Open.
Closed.
Covered.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open.
questions.explanation: Open the fuel valve before you ride. If it is closed, the engine may start using fuel left in the lines, but it will stall when that fuel runs out.

questions.question: Which lane position best prevents other vehicles from sharing your lane?

options.text: The left portion of the lane
The center portion of the lane
The right portion of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion of the lane
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to discourage other drivers from squeezing in next to you. When riding behind a car, the center position puts you in the middle of the driver's rearview mirror, where they are most likely to see you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn
No left turn
No U-turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn
questions.explanation: This regulatory sign is white with red and black markings. It tells drivers what traffic laws apply in that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, make sure it:

options.text: Has no cracks or damage.
Looks nice.
Fits loosely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has no cracks or damage.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state safety standards. It should fit snugly and have no visible damage like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: To reduce your chance of an accident, you should:

options.text: Only ride in the afternoon.
Follow the vehicle in front of you as closely as possible.
Not look ahead and focus only on your controls.
Tell other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: To avoid a crash, make sure other drivers can see you. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Should only be used in an emergency.
Should be used with the rear brake.
Is unsafe to use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be used with the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of these, except:

options.text: Give you an escape route.
Expose you to wind blasts.
Show other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expose you to wind blasts.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It helps you avoid wind blasts, other drivers' blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Help you blend in with traffic.
Give you an escape route.
Invite others to use your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you an escape route.
questions.explanation: Good lane position has many benefits. It helps you see others and be seen. It helps you avoid wind blasts, other drivers' blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: The faster you drink alcohol:

options.text: The faster it leaves your body.
The faster it builds up in your body.
The less it affects your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: The faster it builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: Drinking fast causes alcohol to build up in your body quickly. Your body removes alcohol at about one drink per hour. If you drink more than one drink in an hour, alcohol will still be in your body after that hour.
